title: Audio Fundamentals — Waveforms, Sampling, Fourier Transform
service: WavLab: an audio intake with a 16-bit PCM codec, archive WAV files, tone detection, streaming downsampling and a RIFF chunk walker

parts.lesson_anchor: Bit depth; Build It Step 2 and code/main.py write_wav/read_wav (16-bit PCM)
planted_bugs: float_to_pcm16 clips the float to [-1, 1] before scaling by 32768, so 1.0 becomes 32768; the struct.error surfaces one call later in encode_pcm16
decode_pcm16 slices planar channel blocks instead of de-interleaving L R L R frames (the lesson's read_wav only handles mono)
float_to_pcm16 truncates with int() instead of rounding, as the lesson's write_wav does
encode_pcm16 rebuilds the whole list for every frame, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: 40,000 samples encoded in under 0.12 s (quadratic version about 1.6 s, fixed version about 7 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: every int16 value survives decode then encode, which rules out writing with a 32767 scale (the lesson's write_wav) to dodge the overflow; float_to_pcm16 is also checked on its own, so clamping inside encode_pcm16 instead of fixing the root cause does not pass

parts.lesson_anchor: Bit depth (16-bit exchange format, 24-bit for music); Build It Steps 1-2, WAV files through the stdlib wave module
parts.exactness: 16- and 24-bit samples round-trip exactly through encode_wav and decode_wav, headers match the stdlib wave module byte for byte, and re-saving a decoded file gives the same bytes
traps: bytes per second and per frame count every channel
24-bit sign extension
sample width kept on the Audio
pad byte after an odd-sized chunk, which the wave module leaves out
RIFF size counts the pad byte, the chunk's own size does not
zip cutting unequal channels to the shortest
8-bit files rejected

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It Steps 3-5: DFT, dominant frequency k * sr / N, aliasing; code walkthrough notes on bin 0 and parabolic interpolation
traps: mean removed before the Hann window (skipping bin 0 is not enough)
parabola through log magnitudes
sign of the vertex offset
alias folds modulo sr, then mirrors at sr / 2 (sr - f fails above sr; subtracting sr once fails above 2 * sr)
silence raises
parts.integration: measured peaks of tones above Nyquist match alias_frequency within 0.5 Hz

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It Step 5 and code/main.py Step 6: low-pass before decimating; Use It: real-time streaming into a 16 kHz model
parts.wire_format: little-endian int16 bytes, decided by the test's b''.join and struct.unpack; no empty messages
traps: a read can end halfway through a sample
FIR history across reads
keep-every-third counted in stream indices
emit each block as soon as it is ready
no empty blocks
bytes, not float lists
samples rounded like float_to_pcm16, within half a step of decimate()

parts.lesson_anchor: the RIFF container behind the WAV files of Build It Steps 1-2 (the stdlib wave reader skips chunks it does not know); Use It: inspect a file before use
traps: lists nest to any depth
a container's payload starts with a 4-byte type, and its offset points at that type
pad bytes at every level
JUNK is a leaf even when it holds an old LIST
a child overrunning its parent raises even when it stays inside the file, a missing final pad byte does not
duplicate chunk ids kept
INFO tags only from LIST:INFO, NUL removed, UTF-8
a blob that does not start with RIFF raises
clarifying_questions: sizes never patched by a streaming recorder

deviations: The WAV header is tested in Part 2, not Part 1: Part 1 stays on the lesson's own sample-level code (scale, rounding, saturation, interleaving), and Part 2 owns the container (header fields, RIFF sizes, pad byte), so header sizes are tested once.

Part 2 adds 24-bit PCM, which the lesson names as the format for music: sign extension and keeping the sample width are this format's own exactness traps, and the stdlib wave module is the byte-for-byte reference.
Part 1's saturation bug is a clip placed before the scaling (1.0 becomes 32768 and struct.pack fails one call later) rather than a wrap; wrapping is checked as a wrong fix.
Part 3 also implements alias_frequency, because the lesson's sr - f only holds between sr / 2 and sr; the test checks the measured peaks against it.
Part 4 streams 16-bit PCM bytes in and out, so a read that ends halfway through a sample is part of the streaming problem.
